title: 'The Blue Hotel,' by Stephen Crane, Part Four
titleZh: 《蓝色的旅馆》，斯蒂芬·克莱恩著，第四部分

sentences.en: The Swede’s face, fresh from Johnnie’s blows, felt more pleasure than pain in the wind and the whipping snow.
sentences.zh: 瑞典人那张脸刚挨过约翰尼的拳打,此刻迎在风和狂舞的雪花里,感觉到的快感竟多于痛楚。

sentences.en: A number of square shapes appeared before him and he recognized them as the houses of the town.
sentences.zh: 眼前浮现出若干方形轮廓,他认出那是镇上的房屋。

sentences.en: He traveled along a street until he found a saloon.
sentences.zh: 他沿着一条街走去,直到找到一家酒馆。

sentences.en: He pushed open the door and entered.
sentences.zh: 他推门走了进去。

sentences.en: At the end of the room four men sat drinking at a table.
sentences.zh: 房间尽头,四个男人正围坐在桌旁饮酒。

sentences.en: The Swede dropped his bag upon the floor and, smiling at the saloon-keeper, said, “Give me some whiskey, will you?”
sentences.zh: 瑞典人把行李往地上一丢,对着酒保笑了笑,说道:"给我点威士忌,行吗?"

sentences.en: The man placed a bottle, a whiskey glass, and a glass of ice-filled water upon a table.
sentences.zh: 酒保放下一瓶威士忌、一只威士忌杯和一杯加满冰块的水,摆在桌上。

sentences.en: The Swede poured himself an extra-large amount of whiskey and drank it down.
sentences.zh: 瑞典人给自己倒了满满一大杯威士忌,一饮而尽。

sentences.en: “Bad night,” remarked the saloon-keeper, without interest.
sentences.zh: "糟糕的夜晚,"酒保漫不经心地说道。

sentences.en: He was acting as though he were not noticing the man, but it could have been seen that he was secretly studying the remains of blood on the Swede’s face.
sentences.zh: 他装作没在意这个人,可明眼人看得出,他其实在暗中打量着瑞典人脸上尚未洗净的血迹。

sentences.en: “Bad night,” he said again.
sentences.zh: "糟糕的夜晚,"他又说了一遍。

sentences.en: “Oh, it’s good enough for me,” replied the Swede, as he poured himself some more whiskey.
sentences.zh: "哦,对我来说,这已经够好了,"瑞典人一边给自己又倒威士忌,一边答道。

sentences.en: “No,” continued the Swede, “this isn’t too bad weather.
sentences.zh: "不,"瑞典人接着说,"这天气并不算太坏。

sentences.en: It’s good enough for me.”
sentences.zh: 对我来说,这已经够好了。"

sentences.en: The large drinks of whiskey made the Swede’s eyes watery, and he breathed a little heavier.
sentences.zh: 一大大杯的威士忌让瑞典人的双眼泛起了水汽,他的呼吸也变得略微急促起来。

sentences.en: “Well, I guess I’ll take another drink,” said the Swede after a while.
sentences.zh: "嗯,我想我再喝一杯吧,"过了一会儿,瑞典人说道。

sentences.en: “Would you like something?”
sentences.zh: "想来点别的吗?"

sentences.en: “No, thanks; I’m not drinking.
sentences.zh: "不了,谢谢;我不喝酒。

sentences.en: How did you hurt your face?”
sentences.zh: 你脸怎么弄伤的?"

sentences.en: The Swede immediately began to talk loudly.
sentences.zh: 瑞典人立刻大声讲了起来。

sentences.en: “Oh, in a fight.
sentences.zh: "哦,是在打架。

sentences.en: I beat the soul out of a man at Scully’s hotel.”
sentences.zh: 我把斯库利酒店里一个人的魂儿都打出来了。"

sentences.en: This caught the interest of the four men at the table.
sentences.zh: 这句话引起了桌上四个人的兴趣。

sentences.en: “Who was it?” asked one.
sentences.zh: "是谁?"一个人问道。

sentences.en: “Johnnie Scully, son of the man who owns the hotel.
sentences.zh: "约翰尼·斯库利,就是那家酒店的老板的儿子。

sentences.en: He will be nearly dead for some weeks, I can tell you, I beat him well, I did.
sentences.zh: 我告诉你,他得躺上几个星期,我把他打得够呛,真的。

sentences.en: He couldn’t get up.
sentences.zh: 他爬不起来。

sentences.en: They had to carry him into the house.
sentences.zh: 他们把他抬进了屋里。

sentences.en: Have a drink?”
sentences.zh: 喝一杯吗?"

sentences.en: Instantly the men in a quiet way surrounded themselves in privacy.
sentences.zh: 立刻,那些人以安静的方式把自己围在私密空间里。

sentences.en: “No, thanks,” said one.
sentences.zh: "不了,谢谢,"一个人说。

sentences.en: It was a strange group.
sentences.zh: 这是一群奇怪的人。

sentences.en: Two were well-known local businessmen; one was a lawyer; and one was a gambler.
sentences.zh: 其中两个是当地有名的商人,一个是律师,还有一个是赌徒。

sentences.en: But a close look at the group would not have enabled an observer to pick the gambler from the other men.
sentences.zh: 但仔细观察这群人,观察者也无法从其他人中分辨出谁是赌徒。

sentences.en: He was, in fact, so delicate in manner and so careful with whom he gambled that the men of the town completely trusted and admired him.
sentences.zh: 事实上,他的举止如此文雅,而且赌博时如此谨慎地选择对手,以至于镇上的男人都完全信任和钦佩他。

sentences.en: His business was regarded with fear and lack of respect.
sentences.zh: 他的生意令人畏惧,也得不到尊重。

sentences.en: That is why, without doubt, his quiet dignity shone brightly above the quiet dignity of men who might be merely hat-makers, or builders or salesmen.
sentences.zh: 正因如此,他那沉静的尊严无疑要高于那些可能只是制帽匠、建筑商或推销员的沉静尊严。

sentences.en: Beyond an occasional unwise traveler who came by rail, this gambler supposedly cheated only careless farmers who, when rich with good crops, drove into town full of foolish pride.
sentences.zh: 除了偶尔有乘坐火车路过的不明智的旅客,这个赌徒据说是专门骗那些粗心的农民,而这些农民在丰收致富时,会带着愚蠢的骄傲满满当当地开车进城。

sentences.en: Hearing at times of such a farmer, the important men of Romper usually laughed at his losses.
sentences.zh: 有时听到这样的农民,罗姆佩尔镇上的要人们通常会嘲笑他的损失。

sentences.en: And if they thought of the gambler at all, it was with a kind of pride of knowing he would never dare to attack their wisdom and courage.
sentences.zh: 而如果他们想起这个赌徒,那也是带着一种骄傲,知道他从不敢挑战他们的智慧和勇气。

sentences.en: Besides, it was known that this gambler had a wife and two children in a nice little house, where he led a perfect home life.
sentences.zh: 此外，人们知道这个赌徒在漂亮的小房子里有妻子和两个孩子，过着美满的家庭生活。

sentences.en: And when anyone even suggested that there was a fault in his character, the men immediately described the virtues of his family life.
sentences.zh: 而当有人甚至暗示他性格上有缺陷时，这些人立刻大谈他家庭生活的种种美德。

sentences.en: And one must not forget to declare the bare fact of his entire position in Romper.
sentences.zh: 人们还不应忘记声明他在罗姆珀尔的全部处境这一赤裸裸的事实。

sentences.en: It is true that in all affairs other than his business, this card-player was so generous, so fair, so good, that he could be considered to have a higher moral sense than nine-tenths of the citizens of Romper.
sentences.zh: 确实，除了生意上的事，这个打牌的人在一切事务上都如此慷慨、如此公正、如此善良，以至于可以认为他的道德感比罗姆珀尔十分之九的市民都要高。

sentences.en: And so it happened that he was seated in this saloon with two local businessmen and the lawyer.
sentences.zh: 于是，他便和两个当地商人以及那位律师一起坐在这间酒馆里。

sentences.en: The Swede continued to drink whiskey and to try to make the saloon-keeper drink with him. “Come on.
sentences.zh: 那个瑞典人继续喝着威士忌，并试图让酒馆老板和他一起喝。“来吧。

sentences.en: Have a drink. Come on. No?
sentences.zh: 喝一杯。来吧。不？

sentences.en: Well, have a little one, then.
sentences.zh: 那么，就喝一小杯吧。

sentences.en: By God, I’ve beaten a man tonight, and I beat him good, too!
sentences.zh: 天哪，我今晚会赢一个人，而且把他赢得很惨！

sentences.en: Gentlemen,” the Swede cried to the men at the table, “have a drink?”
sentences.zh: “先生们，”瑞典人对桌旁的男人们喊道，“喝一杯吗？”

sentences.en: Quiet!” said the saloon-keeper.
sentences.zh: “安静！”酒馆老板说。

sentences.en: The group at the table, although really interested, had been trying to appear busy in talk.
sentences.zh: 桌旁的那群人虽然真的很感兴趣，却一直在努力显得在谈话中很忙。

sentences.en: But now a man lifted his eyes toward the Swede and said shortly, “Thanks.
sentences.zh: 但现在有一个人把目光投向瑞典人，简短地说：“谢谢。

sentences.en: We don’t want any more.”
sentences.zh: 我们不要再了。”

sentences.en: At this reply, the Swede straightened.
sentences.zh: 听到这个回答，瑞典人直起身子。

sentences.en: “Well,” he shouted, “it seems I can’t get anybody to drink with me.
sentences.zh: “好吧，”他喊道，“看来没人愿意和我喝酒。

sentences.en: I want someone to drink with me now. Now!
sentences.zh: 我现在想要有人和我喝酒。现在！

sentences.en: Do you understand?”
sentences.zh: 你明白了吗？”

sentences.en: He struck the table with his hand.
sentences.zh: 他用拳头敲了敲桌子。

sentences.en: Years of experience had hardened the saloon-keeper.
sentences.zh: 多年的经验使酒馆老板变得 hardened。

sentences.en: He merely answered, “I hear you.”
sentences.zh: 他只是回答：“我听见了。”

sentences.en: “Well,” cried the Swede, “listen then.
sentences.zh: “那么，”瑞典人大喊道，“听着。

sentences.en: See those men over there?
sentences.zh: 看见那边那些男人了吗？

sentences.en: Well, they’re going to drink with me, and don’t you forget it.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他们要跟我一起喝酒，你可别忘了。

sentences.en: Now you watch.”
sentences.zh: 现在你看着。”

sentences.en: “Stop that!” shouted the saloon-keeper.
sentences.zh: “住手！”酒馆老板喊道。

sentences.en: “Why should I?” demanded the Swede.
sentences.zh: “我为什么要住手？”瑞典人问道。

sentences.en: He walked to the men’s table, and by chance laid his hand on the shoulder of the gambler.
sentences.zh: 他走到那群男人的桌旁，碰巧把手搭在那个赌徒的肩上。

sentences.en: “What about it?” he asked angrily.
sentences.zh: “你说什么？”他生气地问。

sentences.en: “I asked you to drink with me.”
sentences.zh: “我请你跟我一起喝酒。”

sentences.en: The gambler simply turned his head and spoke over his shoulder.
sentences.zh: 赌徒只是转过头，从肩膀后面开口说话。

sentences.en: “My friend, I don’t know you.”
sentences.zh: “我的朋友，我不认识你。”

sentences.en: “Never mind!” answered the Swede.
sentences.zh: “没关系！”瑞典人回答。

sentences.en: “Come and have a drink.”
sentences.zh: “过来一起喝杯酒。”

sentences.en: “Now, my boy,” advised the gambler kindly, “take your hand off my shoulder and go away.”
sentences.zh: “现在，孩子，”赌徒和蔼地劝道，“把手从我肩上拿开，然后走开。”

sentences.en: He was a little, thin man and it seemed strange to hear him use this tone to the big Swede.
sentences.zh: 他是个又小又瘦的男人，听起来用这种语气对那个高大的瑞典人说话显得很奇怪。

sentences.en: The other men at the table said nothing.
sentences.zh: 桌上其他男人一句话也没说。

sentences.en: “What!
sentences.zh: “什么？

sentences.en: You won’t drink with me, you little fool?
sentences.zh: 你不肯跟我一起喝酒，你这个小傻瓜？

sentences.en: I’ll make you then!
sentences.zh: 那我可要教训教训你了！”

sentences.en: I’ll make you!”
sentences.zh: 我要让你付出代价！”

sentences.en: The Swede had grasped the gambler fiercely at the throat, and was dragging him from his chair.
sentences.zh: 瑞典人猛地掐住那个赌徒的喉咙，把他从椅子上拖了起来。

sentences.en: The other men jumped up.
sentences.zh: 其他男子跳了起来。

sentences.en: The saloon-keeper ran toward the table.
sentences.zh: 酒馆老板朝桌子跑去。

sentences.en: There was a great scene of shouts and movements, and then a long knife appeared in the hand of the gambler.
sentences.zh: 一时间吵喊声和骚动声一片，接着赌徒手里出现了一把长刀。

sentences.en: It shot forward, and a human body was cut as easily as if it had been a piece of fruit.
sentences.zh: 刀猛地刺出，一个人的身体被轻易地切开，就像切开一件水果。

sentences.en: The Swede fell with a cry of greatest surprise.
sentences.zh: 瑞典人发出一声极度惊讶的呼喊，倒了下来。

sentences.en: The businessmen and the lawyer must have rushed out of the place backward.
sentences.zh: 商人们和律师一定倒退着冲出了那个地方。

sentences.en: The saloon-keeper found himself hanging weakly to the arm of a chair and gazing into the eyes of a murderer.
sentences.zh: 酒馆老板发现自己虚弱地挂在椅子扶手上，正凝视着一个杀手的眼睛。

sentences.en: “Henry,” said the latter, “you tell them where to find me.
sentences.zh: “亨利，”后者说道，“你告诉他们到哪里来找我。

sentences.en: I’ll be home waiting.”
sentences.zh: 我会在家等着。”

sentences.en: Then he left.
sentences.zh: 然后他就离开了。

sentences.en: A moment afterward the saloon-keeper was in the street racing through the storm for help and, more important, companionship.
sentences.zh: 片刻之后，酒馆老板冲上街头，在暴风雨中飞奔去寻求帮助，更重要的是寻找同伴。

sentences.en: Months later, the cowboy was cooking meat on the stove of a small cattle farm near the Dakota border when there was the sound of a horse stopping outside.
sentences.zh: 几个月后，那个牛仔正在达科他边境附近一处小型牧场里的炉子上烤肉，这时外面传来马停下的声音。

sentences.en: The Easterner entered with mail and newspapers.
sentences.zh: 东部人带着邮件和报纸走了进来。

sentences.en: “Well,” said the Easterner at once, “the fellow who killed the Swede will spend three years in prison.
sentences.zh: “好吧，”东部人立刻说道，“那个杀死瑞典人的人将在监狱里度过三年。

sentences.en: That’s not much, is it?”
sentences.zh: 这不算多，不是吗？”

sentences.en: “He will? Three years!”
sentences.zh: “他会？三年！”

sentences.en: The cowboy turned the meat in the pan. “Three years.
sentences.zh: 牛仔在锅里翻动着肉。“三年。

sentences.en: That isn’t much.”
sentences.zh: 这并不多。”

sentences.en: “No,” replied the Easterner.
sentences.zh: “不，”东部人回答说。

sentences.en: “There was a lot of sympathy for him in Romper.”
sentences.zh: “在罗姆珀，很多人对他都抱有同情。”

sentences.en: “If the saloon-keeper had been any good,” said cowboy thoughtfully, “he would have gone in and hit that Swede on the head with a bottle in the beginning of it.
sentences.zh: “如果那酒馆老板有点本事，”牛仔若有所思地说，“他一开始就该冲进去，拿瓶子砸那个瑞典人的脑袋。

sentences.en: That would have stopped all this murdering.”
sentences.zh: 那样就能阻止这一切的杀戮了。”

sentences.en: “Yes, a thousand things might have happened,” said the Easterner sharply.
sentences.zh: “是啊，本来可能发生一千种事情，”东部人尖刻地说。

sentences.en: The cowboy moved his pan of meat on the fire, continued with his philosophy.
sentences.zh: 牛仔把锅里的肉在火上挪了挪，继续发表他的议论。

sentences.en: “It’s strange, isn’t it?
sentences.zh: “很奇怪，是不是？

sentences.en: If he hadn’t said Johnnie was cheating, he’d be alive this minute.
sentences.zh: 如果他没说是约翰尼在作弊，他这会儿还活着呢。

sentences.en: He was an awful fool.
sentences.zh: 他真是个天大的蠢货。

sentences.en: I believe he was crazy.”
sentences.zh: 我相信他当时是疯了。”

sentences.en: “I feel sorry for that gambler,” said the Easterner.
sentences.zh: “我为那个赌徒感到难过，”东部人说。

sentences.en: “So do I,” said the cowboy.
sentences.zh: “我也是，”牛仔说。

sentences.en: “He doesn’t deserve three years in prison for killing that fellow.”
sentences.zh: “他为了杀那个人被判三年徒刑，实在罪不当罚。”

sentences.en: “The Swede might not have been killed if everything had been honest.”
sentences.zh: “如果一切都光明磊落，那个瑞典人也许就不会被杀。”

sentences.en: “Might not have been killed?” exclaimed the cowboy. “Everything honest?
sentences.zh: “就不会被杀？”牛仔惊呼起来。“光明磊落？

sentences.en: When he said that Johnnie was cheating and acted so crazy?
sentences.zh: 他说约翰尼作弊，还表现得那么疯狂？

sentences.en: And then in the saloon he practically asked to get hurt?”
sentences.zh: 接着在酒馆里，他几乎等于自找打？”

sentences.en: With these arguments the cowboy made the Easterner angry.
sentences.zh: 靠着这些论据，牛仔把东部人惹怒了。

sentences.en: “You’re a fool!” cried the Easterner fiercely.
sentences.zh: “你才是个蠢货！”东部人愤怒地喊道。

sentences.en: “You’re a bigger fool than that Swede.
sentences.zh: “你比那个瑞典人更是个蠢货。

sentences.en: Now let me tell you one thing.
sentences.zh: 现在让我告诉你一件事。

sentences.en: Let me tell you one thing. Listen!
sentences.zh: 让我告诉你一件事。听着！

sentences.en: Johnnie was cheating!”
sentences.zh: 约翰尼在作弊！”

sentences.en: “Johnnie,” said the cowboy, blankly.
sentences.zh: “约翰尼，”牛仔茫然地说。

sentences.en: There was a minute of silence, and then he said strongly, “Oh, no.
sentences.zh: 有一分钟的沉默，然后他坚定地说：“哦，不。

sentences.en: The game was only for fun.”
sentences.zh: 游戏只是为了好玩。”

sentences.en: “Fun or not,” said the Easterner, “Johnnie was cheating.
sentences.zh: “好玩还是不好玩，”东部人说，“约翰尼在作弊。

sentences.en: I saw him.
sentences.zh: 我看到了。

sentences.en: I know it.
sentences.zh: 我知道。

sentences.en: I saw him.
sentences.zh: 我看到了。

sentences.en: And I refused to stand up and be a man.
sentences.zh: 而我拒绝站起来做一个男人。

sentences.en: I let the Swede fight alone.
sentences.zh: 我让瑞典人独自战斗。

sentences.en: And you—you were simply jumping around the place and wanting to fight.
sentences.zh: 而你——你只是在这个地方跳来跳去，想要战斗。

sentences.en: And old Scully too.
sentences.zh: 老萨利也是。

sentences.en: We are all in it!
sentences.zh: 我们都参与其中！

sentences.en: This poor gambler just got pulled into it.
sentences.zh: 这个可怜的赌徒只是被卷了进来。

sentences.en: Every sin is the result of shared effort.
sentences.zh: 每一条罪都是共同努力的结果。

sentences.en: We, five of us, have shared in the murder of this Swede.
sentences.zh: 我们五个人共同参与了这场对瑞典人的谋杀。

sentences.en: You, I, Johnnie, old Scully; and that fool of an unfortunate gambler came merely at the end of a human movement, and gets all the punishment.”
sentences.zh: 你、我、约翰尼、老萨利；还有那个愚蠢的不幸运的赌徒，他只是出现在最后的人类行动中，却承担了所有的惩罚。”

sentences.en: The cowboy, hurt and angry, cried out blindly into this mystery of thought: “Well, I didn’t do anything, did I?”
sentences.zh: 牛仔既受伤又愤怒，盲目地对着这思想的奥秘喊道：“嗯，我什么都没做，不是吗？”

glossary.def: a place where alcoholic drinks are served
a strong alcoholic drink made from a grain (such as rye, corn, or barley)
a person whose job is to guide and assist people in matters relating to the law
a person who plays a game in which he/she can win or lose money or other valuable things
the ability to do something that you know is difficult or dangerous
a bad quality or part of someone’s character
the way someone thinks, feels, and behaves; someone's personality
cows, bulls, or steers that are kept on a farm or ranch for meat or milk
an action that is considered to be wrong according to religious or moral law
